challenges.name: feature-flags-quiz
challenges.title: Read the batch-delivery rollout
challenges.description: Three statements about how Rice Rocket shipped the batch-delivery screen to its couriers, and what happened when it crashed. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: A staged rollout decides who can download a release. What does it change for a phone that has already installed it?
Run the bucketing twice for the same courier in your head: does the courier land in the same group on the next launch?
Think about the very first launch on a phone with no network: where do the flag values come from before any fetch succeeds?

questions.question:
Version 2.5.0 had the batch-delivery screen switched on in code. It went out as a 20% staged rollout and crashed on some phones:

```text
Play Console  2.5.0  Production  staged rollout 20%  -> halted 14:10
Crashlytics   BatchDeliveryScreen  NullPointerException  1,240 users  (still rising at 16:00)
```

Statement: "Halting the staged rollout removes 2.5.0 from the phones that already installed it, so the crash count stops rising at once."
questions.explanation: False. Halting a staged rollout stops new users from getting the release; phones that already updated keep 2.5.0 until a newer version reaches them, which takes a release plus days of update adoption. That is why the crash count kept rising. A feature behind a remote flag with a kill switch could have been turned off for every phone within minutes, without a release.

questions.question:
The first flag client decided the rollout with a random draw at every launch:

```kotlin
val batchOn = Random.nextInt(100) < remote.getLong("batch_percent")
```

```text
courier c-118: 08:02 launch batch ON, 11:40 launch batch OFF, 13:15 launch batch ON
support ticket: "the screen keeps changing, where did my batch go?"
```

Statement: "Bucketing must be stable per courier, for example a hash of the flag key and the courier id mod 100, so a courier stays in the same group on every launch while another flag splits couriers differently."
questions.explanation: True. A rollout percentage only means something if each courier gets the same answer every time: hash(flagKey + courierId) mod 100 gives a fixed bucket per courier and flag, raising the percentage only adds couriers, and including the flag key keeps different experiments from always picking the same people. A random draw per launch flips couriers between screens mid-shift.

questions.question:
The in-app defaults for remote config were copied from the console, where the flag was on:

```kotlin
remoteConfig.setDefaultsAsync(mapOf("batch_enabled" to true))
```

```text
first launch after install, no network in the warehouse basement
remote config fetch failed: no connectivity -> using defaults
BatchDeliveryScreen shown  (flag was set to false in the console at 14:12)
```

Statement: "In-app defaults must be the safe value, off for a risky feature, because a phone that cannot fetch runs on its defaults."
questions.explanation: True. Remote values arrive only after a successful fetch; until then, and on every launch where the fetch fails, the app uses the defaults compiled into it. A default of true turns the kill switch into a no-op for offline couriers. Ship risky features off by default and let the fetched value turn them on.

challenges.name: feature-flag-evaluation
challenges.title: Evaluate feature flags on the phone
challenges.description: The courier app decides on the phone which features a courier gets, from flags fetched with remote config. The editor holds `Flags.kt` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that the checks run in this order: a killed flag (`enabled=false`) is off for everyone, QA couriers included; a courier whose app is older than `minVersion` (compared number by number, so 2.10.0 is newer than 2.9.0, and 2.4 equals 2.4.0) or whose Android SDK is below `minSdk` is off; a courier on the QA allowlist is on; everyone else is on when their bucket is below `percent`, where bucket = (FNV-1a 32 of `<flagKey>:<courierId>` and 0x7fffffff) mod 100. The runner prints every flag's decision for every courier with its reason.
hints: Take one courier through every check in order and write down which one decides. Then ask what each check is protecting: crashes on old apps and phones, the kill switch, a stable split.

Look at `compareVersions` (split on dots, compare numbers, missing parts count as 0), `bucket` (the hash input decides whether two flags pick the same couriers), and where the allowlist sits relative to the kill switch.

An A/B test of a checkout button in a shop app: `fun group(test: String, user: String) = (fnv1a32("$test:$user") and 0x7fffffff) % 100`, `if (!test.running) return CONTROL`, `if (compareVersions(app, test.minApp) < 0) return CONTROL`, `if (user in test.forced) return VARIANT`, `return if (group(test.key, user) < test.percent) VARIANT else CONTROL`.
